survivingClaim: Precise obstruction; family closed; nothing about zeta zeros. For unimodular completely multiplicative chi with S(x) not o(x), power-saving additive twists with no main term at prime moduli force chi = n^(-i alpha) (chi = 1 if the main term is cx) via sum_{a mod p} T(x;a/p) = p chi(p) S(x/p); the hypothesis is then classical. With S(x) = o(x) the strict hypothesis is the strip hypothesis itself (circular). With main terms allowed, THIN passes (error O(q x^(b+eps)) proved; about x^0.4-0.5 measured for random members with a zero at b, q<=103, x<=1e10 author and x<=1e8 referee) and fails the strict form (main term -2cx/(p-1), proved and reproduced). For real chi the twisted series equals L(s,psi) exp(-A(s,psi)) right of sigma_0 with no twisted hypothesis. Greedy discrepancy exponent well below b is measured and is consistent with the parent Theorem 1. Status: author-checked plus one referee (general lens).
obstruction: Strict form (no main term at q > 1): sum over a mod p of the twisted sums equals p chi(p) S(x/p), so any theta < 1 forces chi = n^(-i alpha) (chi = 1 if the main term is cx): an identification with no inequality; with S(x) = o(x) the hypothesis is the strip hypothesis itself. General form (main terms allowed): THIN passes with error O(q x^(b+eps)) (proved) and has a zero at b. For real chi the twisted series equals L(s,psi) exp(-A(s,psi)) right of sigma_0 without any twisted hypothesis. One referee; Lemma A step (c) to be refereed.

lesson: Modulus-uniform additive-twist hypotheses on a unimodular completely multiplicative chi are either an identification (strict form: only n^(-i alpha) passes, at any theta<1) or passed by THIN (general form). Periodicity of twists separates zeta from THIN and Beurling but carries no inequality. Separately: the greedy THIN set is biased in residue classes (mod 3 imbalance 26000 of 1.02e6 at 1e8), giving twisted errors near x^0.8; the random set does not show this.
